Iterate source.headers for column order. Visible text #row-count must show only the number of displayed rows, never an input. Input #filter filters immediately by exact source_row string; empty displays all rows; unknown string displays zero rows. Button #reset clears the filter and restores all rows. Table headers remain present even when zero rows match. All cells and controls must be visible (scrolling for long tables is allowed). Render exact visible #scope text: Recorded or declared data; quality flags retained. Not a new physical measurement. Render exact visible #data-quality text: Within declared thresholds. Use a readable responsive teal design with scrollable table and wrapping controls. Keep code concise. Java owns the fixed checks and independently compares actual cells and controls after rendering. User intent, subject to that fixed source contract: Analyze the selected dataset, create a verified java summary report. Use gap limit 0.05 seconds and speed limit 5 m/s. This is a motion SUMMARY REPORT. Preserve every table, filter and quality requirement above. Above the scrollable table, show visible summary cards with the following exact numeric text and IDs (no units inside these values): {"summary-travel":"0.775845","summary-speeds":"0","summary-samples":"49","summary-peak":"3.866609","summary-duration":"0.800000","summary-gaps":"0"}. These object keys are the complete DOM IDs, including the summary- prefix. IDs are #summary-samples, #summary-duration, #summary-travel, #summary-peak, #summary-gaps, #summary-speeds. Put units in separate labels: samples, duration seconds, travel metres, peak speed m/s, gap flags, speed flags. Values are derived from the complete source; filtering changes the table only, never the summary or chart. Add one visible native SVG id=motion-plot, viewBox='0 0 640 240', width=100%, with one direct-child polyline id=motion-trace, fill=none, visible stroke width2. No transform attribute or CSS transform on the SVG or polyline. Use all original source.rows in order: t=Number(row.time_s), d=Number(row.displacement_m). t0=first t; tn=last t; lo=Math.min(0,...all d); hi=Math.max(0,...all d). Each actual SVG point must be x=40+560*(t-t0)/(tn-t0), y=200-160*(d-lo)/Math.max(1e-12,hi-lo). Do not smooth, subsample or invent points. Flat traces must remain visible. Show exact visible labels #time-axis='Time (s)' and #distance-axis='Displacement (m)'. SVG trace and all summary values remain unchanged in all four filter states. Keep the whole report compact and readable; scroll long tables. Use original source-derived values, not a screenshot or hardcoded trace.

input.request: Analyze the selected dataset, create a verified java summary report. Use gap limit 0.05 seconds and speed limit 5 m/s.

Build a compact working motion-data explorer with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, no libraries. Load inputs/source.json with fetch. Render the source title in #title. Use TABLE id=data-table with thead/tr/th and tbody/tr/td. Exact headers in order: source_row, time_s, displacement_m. Every row in source order, every original source string unchanged via textContent. Do not round or append units inside cells; explain seconds and metres in a caption. Iterate source.headers for column order. Visible text #row-count must show only the number of displayed rows, never an input. Input #filter filters immediately by exact source_row string; empty displays all rows; unknown string displays zero rows. Button #reset clears the filter and restores all rows. Table headers remain present even when zero rows match. All cells and controls must be visible (scrolling for long tables is allowed). Render exact visible #scope text: Recorded or declared data; quality flags retained. Not a new physical measurement. Render exact visible #data-quality text: Within declared thresholds. Use a readable responsive teal design with scrollable table and wrapping controls. Keep code concise. Java owns the fixed checks and independently compares actual cells and controls after rendering. User intent, subject to that fixed source contract: Analyze the selected dataset, create a verified java summary report. Use gap limit 0.05 seconds and speed limit 5 m/s. This is a motion SUMMARY REPORT. Preserve every table, filter and quality requirement above. Above the scrollable table, show visible summary cards with the following exact numeric text and IDs (no units inside these values): {"summary-travel":"0.726476","summary-speeds":"0","summary-samples":"52","summary-peak":"2.067490","summary-duration":"0.850000","summary-gaps":"0"}. These object keys are the complete DOM IDs, including the summary- prefix. IDs are #summary-samples, #summary-duration, #summary-travel, #summary-peak, #summary-gaps, #summary-speeds. Put units in separate labels: samples, duration seconds, travel metres, peak speed m/s, gap flags, speed flags. Values are derived from the complete source; filtering changes the table only, never the summary or chart. Add one visible native SVG id=motion-plot, viewBox='0 0 640 240', width=100%, with one direct-child polyline id=motion-trace, fill=none, visible stroke width2. No transform attribute or CSS transform on the SVG or polyline. Use all original source.rows in order: t=Number(row.time_s), d=Number(row.displacement_m). t0=first t; tn=last t; lo=Math.min(0,...all d); hi=Math.max(0,...all d). Each actual SVG point must be x=40+560*(t-t0)/(tn-t0), y=200-160*(d-lo)/Math.max(1e-12,hi-lo). Do not smooth, subsample or invent points. Flat traces must remain visible. Show exact visible labels #time-axis='Time (s)' and #distance-axis='Displacement (m)'. SVG trace and all summary values remain unchanged in all four filter states. Keep the whole report compact and readable; scroll long tables. Use original source-derived values, not a screenshot or hardcoded trace.

java.scope: Diagnostic wall spans only. Inclusive nested spans overlap; exclusive time is within one Java thread. Native checks include their original report/source checks. Do not add Java and browser spans as independent time. Restart starts a new epoch; diagnostics never authorize outcomes.

browser.scope: Diagnostic actual canvas navigation, assertion and observation spans. Nested inclusive spans overlap; exclusive spans subtract the union of completed child intervals. Detached children are counted separately. Browser and Java wall spans can overlap; do not sum them as total task time. No acceptance result is inferred from timing.

recording.scope: Process-local recording reconstruction only. Every use rereads original image, metadata, labels, calibration, historical-world and code evidence before and after. Cold or changed evidence reconstructs. Native and outcome checks are never memoized here.
